specs.title: CSV export of reports
sources: Owner request: let users export reports as CSV
Reports page as it is today: table with columns Date, Region, Orders, Revenue; date range filter
in_scope: Users can download the reports table as a CSV file
The file's header row is Date, Region, Orders, Revenue, in that order
non_goals: Changes to the table's columns or filters

criteria.text: Given the reports page, when the user chooses Export CSV, then a CSV file downloads whose header row is Date, Region, Orders, Revenue.
criteria.check: Integration test on fixture data; compare the header row with the expected one.

criteria.text: Given a date range is applied, when the user chooses Export CSV, then the data rows are the rows the rule in open question 1 selects.
criteria.check: Integration test with a fixed date range; compare row count and values with the expected set. Blocked until open question 1 is answered.

criteria.text: Given a user who is not allowed to export, when the user chooses Export CSV, then no file is produced and the user sees a clear message.
criteria.check: Negative test with a user without the permission. Blocked until open question 2 is answered.

criteria.text: Given a date range with no matching rows, when the user chooses Export CSV, then the file contains the header row only.
criteria.check: Test with an empty range. Blocked until open question 1 is answered.

expected_areas: Reports page and its data endpoint

open_questions.question: Does the export contain the rows the filtered table shows, or every row of the report?

options.changes: Export depends on the date filter state
Export ignores the filter; files can be much larger

open_questions.question: Who may export reports: every user who can see the reports page, or a restricted group?

options.changes: No new permission check
A new permission with its own checks and messages

open_questions.question: Is there a maximum number of rows per export?

options.changes: Large exports may time out, as seen in the later QA report on version 2

options.option: A stated limit with a message
options.changes: A new criterion for the limit and its message

versions: 1 (draft): first version; awaiting owner answers to the open questions

actions_now: Write the draft with the header criteria and the no-row-filter-independent parts now, and put the three open questions to the owner. Nothing is approved; criteria 2 to 4 wait for the answers.

specs.title: Discount at checkout
sources: Owner request: add a discount to checkout
Binding: provisional choices are not allowed for prices (so no price choice is made here)
in_scope: Checkout can apply a discount to an order
The discount appears in the checkout total
non_goals: Any change to totals of orders that have no discount

criteria.text: Given a checkout with no discount applied, when the total is shown, then the total is the same as before this change.
criteria.check: Regression test of checkout totals against the current behaviour on a fixed set of carts.

open_questions.question: How large is the discount?

options.changes: Criteria state an amount
Criteria state a percentage and rounding rules

open_questions.question: Who receives the discount?

options.changes: No eligibility check
Eligibility rules and a negative criterion for others

open_questions.question: Does the discount combine with other offers?

options.changes: Order of application and the total must be specified
A rule that rejects or chooses between offers

versions: 1 (draft): first version; only the no-discount regression criterion is written; the rest waits for the owner

actions_now: Write the draft with only the regression criterion, since the discount rules are money decisions that no agent may make even provisionally. Put the size, recipient and combination questions to the owner.

Do not edit approved version 1 and do not add customer emails. Ask the owner whether criterion 3 should go into a new version 2 (dropping or re-scoping it, with the change recorded) or be handled by a separate line, noting that customer email is personal data; the implementer continues the other criteria meanwhile.

specs.title: Dashboard load time
sources: Owner request: make the dashboard faster
in_scope: Load time of the Overview, Sales and Inventory views of the dashboard
non_goals: Changes to what the dashboard shows

criteria.text: Given the load time of each view measured now on the same data and with the same method, when the change is measured the same way, then no view is slower than before.
criteria.check: Benchmark recorded before work starts and again after the change, same data set and method.

expected_areas: Dashboard views and their data queries

open_questions.question: What is the target load time for each view, at which percentile, on which data size and device?

options.changes: A single threshold criterion
Three threshold criteria

versions: 1 (draft): first version; the no-regression criterion is written, the target waits for the owner

actions_now: Write the draft with a no-regression criterion measured against a baseline taken before work starts, and ask the owner for targets. No target is invented, so 'fast enough' stays unverified.

specs.title: Theme and language kept across devices
sources: Owner request: users keep theme and language settings across devices
The table name in the request is a suggestion for the architect, not a requirement of this spec
in_scope: A user's theme and language settings belong to the account
They apply on every device where the user signs in
non_goals: Preferences other than theme and language
The storage design, which the architect decides

criteria.text: Given a user has set a language, when the user signs in on a second device, then the second device shows that language.
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions of one account; compare the language shown.

criteria.text: Given a user has set a theme, when the user signs in on a second device, then the second device shows that theme.
criteria.check: Integration test as in criterion 1, for the theme.

criteria.text: Given a user who has never set a theme or language, when the user signs in, then the defaults apply.
criteria.check: Test of a new account against the defaults. Blocked until open question 2 is answered.

criteria.text: Given a value outside the allowed list, when a device tries to save it, then the save is refused and the stored setting is unchanged.
criteria.check: Negative test with a value outside the list. Blocked until open questions 1 and 3 are answered.

expected_areas: Account storage, settings page, sign-in flow

open_questions.question: Which theme values exist?

options.changes: Two allowed values

options.option: Light, dark and follow the device
options.changes: A third value that depends on device settings

open_questions.question: What are the defaults for a new account?

options.option: Fixed defaults set by the owner
options.changes: New users see those values

options.option: Taken from the device at first sign-in
options.changes: Defaults depend on the device

open_questions.question: Which languages can be chosen?

options.option: The languages the app offers today
options.changes: Fixes the allowed list

versions: 1 (draft): first version; awaiting owner answers to the open questions

actions_now: Write the draft with the sync criteria, which the request fixes, and put the value and default questions to the owner. Defaults and allowed values are not derived or chosen here.

specs.title: Dark mode
sources: Draft spec 'Dark mode' written by the product role in this run; criteria and checks unchanged from the draft
versions: 1 (draft, date of the run): first version, no open questions. Status changed to approved-provisional by the coordinating session while the owner is away; recorded in decisions/queue.yaml as waiting for the owner. Content unchanged. Work built on it is marked provisional: true until the owner decides.

actions_now: Record the provisional status and its queue entry in the spec's header, change nothing else, and mark dependent units provisional. The criteria text is not restated in this case, so it must be carried over from the draft as it is.

specs.title: Password reset
sources: Product role's draft 'Password reset' in this run; criteria and checks unchanged from the draft
versions: 1 (draft): first version, awaiting the owner's approval. Not approved by the product role.

actions_now: Give the owner the draft and ask for approval, flagging that a password reset carries security decisions the owner must check, since the draft has no open questions. The implementer does not start until the owner approves, and the criteria text must be carried over unchanged from the draft.

specs.title: Dark mode toggle in settings
sources: Owner request: a dark mode toggle on the settings page that applies to the whole app
Email templates and the printable invoice view exist; the request does not say whether they are included
in_scope: A dark mode toggle on the settings page
The toggle changes the appearance of the app's screens
non_goals: Email templates and the printable invoice view, until the owner answers open question 1

criteria.text: Given the settings page, when the user switches the dark mode toggle on, then every main screen of the app shows the dark appearance without a reload.
criteria.check: UI test that visits each main screen after the toggle is switched on.

criteria.text: Given the toggle is off, when any screen opens, then its appearance is unchanged from before this change.
criteria.check: Visual regression test of each main screen with the toggle off.

criteria.text: Given the toggle is on, when the user signs in again or reloads, then the dark appearance is still on.
criteria.check: Test across a reload and a new session. Blocked until open question 2 is answered.

open_questions.question: Are email templates and the printable invoice view part of 'the whole app'?

options.changes: New criteria for each surface; email clients differ and need their own checks
They become explicit non-goals

open_questions.question: Is the choice kept across sessions and devices?

options.changes: Needs stored state (see the user preferences line)

options.option: Kept only for the current session
options.changes: Criterion 3 changes

actions_now: Write the draft for the settings toggle and the app screens, and put the two scope questions to the owner. Email and print surfaces stay out until the owner decides.

The request already states numbered, testable criteria with checks, so the product role writes no spec for it and passes it to the factory as it stands, for approval through the route the binding names. The product role does not approve it itself.

This is a bug fix with a known cause, which the product-spec skill excludes, so no spec is written. The request goes back to the implementer with the expected behaviour (the existing no-avatar rendering of the profile page) and a regression check for a user without an avatar.

specs.title: Colleagues' last-online time
sources: Team lead request, passed on by the owner without comment: show each user when colleagues were last online
in_scope: The last-online time of a user is shown to that user's colleagues
non_goals: Any change to how activity is recorded
expected_areas: Activity records, user profile or directory views

open_questions.question: Who may see a user's last-online time?

options.changes: Defines colleagues and the visibility rule
A role rule and negative criteria

open_questions.question: Can a user hide their last-online time?

options.changes: A setting, its default, and a criterion for hidden users
No hiding behaviour

open_questions.question: How long is the last-online time kept?

options.changes: A retention criterion and deletion check
No retention criterion

versions: 1 (draft): first version; no criterion is written until visibility is answered

actions_now: Write the draft with no criteria and put the visibility, hiding and retention questions to the owner. This touches privacy, so no provisional choice is made and no criterion is guessed.

Ask the owner, who is present, what should happen when an export would exceed 100,000 rows, with options such as refusing with a message, capping rows, or delivering the file later. Approved version 2 stays unchanged until the answer, then a new version 3 records it.

specs.title: CSV export on the reports page
sources: Owner request: add CSV export to the reports page
in_scope: The reports page offers a CSV download of the report
non_goals: The partner API, which is a separate line and spec

criteria.text: Given the reports page, when the user chooses Export CSV, then a CSV file downloads.
criteria.check: Integration test on fixture data; the file opens and has one row per report row.

expected_areas: Reports page and its data endpoint

open_questions.question: Which columns and rows does the file contain: the table as shown, or every report column?

options.changes: Columns and filter follow the page
A wider file and a new column list

open_questions.question: Who may export?

options.changes: No new permission
A permission and its checks

specs.title: Partner REST API for reports
sources: Owner request: a public REST API that partners can use to fetch the same reports
Planned as a separate line on its own branch
in_scope: A public endpoint through which partners fetch the same reports
non_goals: The CSV export on the reports page, which is a separate spec

open_questions.question: How does a partner authenticate, and who is a partner?

options.changes: Key issue, rotation and revocation criteria

options.option: Other scheme chosen by the owner
options.changes: Different criteria

open_questions.question: Which report data may partners fetch, and is any personal data included?

options.changes: Narrow data scope
Privacy review and a personal-data rule

open_questions.question: What rate limits and versioning apply?

options.changes: Criteria for limits and versions

versions: 1 (draft): first version; no criterion is written until the security and privacy questions are answered by the owner

actions_now: Write two separate draft specs for the two branches. The partner API touches security and privacy, so it is escalated to the owner with no criteria written and no provisional choice made.

specs.title: Report export with reconcilable columns
sources: Owner request: exports must contain every column of the report, so finance can reconcile
Recorded decision dl-009: personal emails never leave the system in any export (stays in force)
in_scope: Exports carry the report's columns so finance can reconcile
non_goals: Any export that contains a personal email address

criteria.text: Given any report export, when the file is produced, then no cell contains a customer's personal email address and no customer email column is present.
criteria.check: Test on a fixture report with a Customer email column; assert no email value in any cell and the column absent or blank per the open question answer.

criteria.text: Given any report export, when the file is produced, then it contains every other column of the report.
criteria.check: Test comparing the header row with the report's columns. Blocked until open question 1 is answered.

open_questions.question: How does finance reconcile without personal emails, given dl-009?

options.changes: Column present but blank

options.option: Replace it with a non-personal customer identifier
options.changes: A new column and a mapping rule
A privacy decision only the owner can make; this spec then changes

versions: 1 (draft): first version; the request conflicts with dl-009, which is not overridden here

actions_now: Write the draft with the email exclusion from dl-009 and put the conflict to the owner, since only the owner can change a privacy decision. The request's 'every column' criterion waits for the answer.
